questions.question: A team wants new developers to ask Copilot questions about the payment rules and receive answers that are grounded in a selected set of files, issues, and notes. The context must be shared with the whole team. Which feature should the team use?

options.why: Correct. A space gathers curated context such as files, issues, notes, and instructions, and it can be shared with a team.
Spark builds micro apps from natural language. It does not provide shared context for questions.
Summaries describe the changes in a pull request.
Content exclusions remove files from Copilot's context instead of curating context.

questions.explanation: Copilot Spaces provide curated, shareable context so that answers are grounded in the same sources.

questions.question: A developer opens a pull request and wants Copilot to draft a description of the changes. What should the developer do?

options.text: Select the Copilot button in the pull request description box
options.why: Correct. The Copilot option in the description box generates a summary of the pull request changes.
This starts a code review that leaves comments. It does not write the description.

options.text: Assign the pull request to Copilot coding agent
options.why: The coding agent works on issues and tasks. It is not used to write a pull request description.

options.text: Run /doc in Copilot Chat in the IDE
options.why: /doc generates documentation comments for code, not a pull request description on GitHub.

questions.explanation: Pull request summaries are generated from the Copilot button in the description box, and the author should review and edit the result.

questions.question: A product manager wants to build a small internal app that tracks discount code usage by describing it in natural language. Which feature and plan combination supports this requirement?

options.text: GitHub Spark with Copilot Pro+ or Copilot Enterprise
options.why: Correct. Spark builds micro apps from natural language and is available on Copilot Pro+ and Copilot Enterprise.
Spark is not included in Copilot Free.
Spaces provide curated context for questions. They do not build apps.

options.text: Copilot pull request summaries with Copilot Pro
options.why: Pull request summaries describe changes. They do not build apps.

questions.explanation: GitHub Spark turns a natural-language description into a working micro app and is available on Copilot Pro+ and Copilot Enterprise.

questions.question: Which TWO types of content can you add to a Copilot Space?

options.why: Correct. Repository files are a common source in a space.
Correct. Issues can be added to a space as context.
Seats are managed in organization settings or through the REST API.
Policies are configured in organization or enterprise settings, not in a space.

questions.explanation: A Copilot Space can include files, issues, notes, and instructions. Seats and policies are administrative settings.

questions.question: A developer generates a Copilot pull request summary. The summary accurately lists the changed files but does not explain why the change was needed. What should the developer do before requesting reviews?

options.text: Edit the description to add the reason for the change and how to test it
options.why: Correct. A summary is generated from the changes and cannot know the business reason, so the author adds it.

options.text: Leave the summary unchanged because Copilot summaries are complete
options.why: A generated summary is a draft and can miss intent, so it should be reviewed and edited.

options.text: Regenerate the summary until it explains the business reason
options.why: Regenerating cannot add information that is not in the changes, such as a decision made in a meeting.

options.text: Ask Copilot code review to approve the summary
options.why: Copilot code review leaves comments on code and does not approve descriptions.

questions.explanation: Copilot can describe what changed. The author is responsible for adding why it changed and how to verify it.
